changes.evidence: PR #45 of the core: - `ofb_core`: new generic `InitTimeoutWords_g` (default 5000); new outputs `Phy_RxResetOnDisc`, `Phy_RxResetCdrOnly`, `Phy_CdrHoldIdle`, `Phy_PcsRsvdIn`, `Phy_RxResetCmd`; new inputs with default 0 `Phy_RxBufErr`, `Phy_TxBufErr`, `Phy_RxResetDone`, `Phy_RxResetBusy`, `Phy_CdrLock`, `Phy_RxElecIdle`, `Phy_EvRxReset`, `Phy_EvRxResetTimeout`. - `ofb_pa_gty`: new generics `RxRstDoneCycles_g`, `CdrWaitCycles_g`, `RxRstGapCycles_g`; new configuration inputs with defaults, command input and status outputs; new source `src/ofb_pa_gty_lane_rst.vhd` in both compile orders. - `ofb_lane`, `ofb_lane_init` (internal): generic `InitTimeoutWords_g` replaced by the input `Cfg_InitTimeout`. - Register map version 9 to 10 (ID 0x0FB1000A); every new field was reserved in version 9; `sw/ofb_regs.h` regenerated. - Open Logic pin unchanged (4.7.0-ft.9). The merge commit is the release v0.1.3 of the core.

changes.text: New generic InitTimeoutWords_g (default 5000, the timeout of the standard): reset value of the new register LANE_INIT_TIMEOUT, the initialisation timeout of the lanes in lane clock cycles (CORE-PL-08).

Register map version 10 (ID 0x0FB1000A): new registers LANE_INIT_TIMEOUT at 0x07C and PA_CTRL at 0x080; LANE_CTRL bit 18 RX_RESET, LANE_STATUS bits 27:24, LANE_EVENTS bits 7:4, LANE_TIMEOUT_COUNT bits 31:16 RX_RESETS, IRQ_MASK bits 23:16.

The Phy interface carries the receiver reset of the physical adapter: the configuration of PA_CTRL (rx_reset_on_disc, rx_reset_cdr_only, cdr_hold_idle, pcs_rsvd_in, asynchronous levels), the receiver reset command of LANE_CTRL (rx_reset_cmd) and the status and events of the adapter per lane (rx_buf_err, tx_buf_err, rx_reset_done, rx_reset_busy, cdr_lock, rx_elec_idle, ev_rx_reset, ev_rx_reset_timeout). A connected ofb_pa_gty drives them; an external Phy interface has them as top-level ports.
New generic RxRstDoneCycles_g (default 15000000, 150 ms at 100 MHz): bound of the wait for RXRESETDONE in an entire receiver reset, in cycles of FreeRunClk (PA-RS-05).
New generic CdrWaitCycles_g (default 10000, 100 us at 100 MHz): wait after the RXCDRRESET pulse of the CDR-only receiver reset, in cycles of FreeRunClk.

New generic RxRstGapCycles_g (default 400000, 4 ms at 100 MHz): gap after a receiver reset of a lane in which further requests are dropped (PA-RS-04); 0 for a design whose initialisation timeout is longer than a receiver reset.

The Phy interface carries the new configuration inputs (Cfg_RxResetOnDisc, Cfg_RxResetCdrOnly, Cfg_CdrHoldIdle, Cfg_PcsRsvdIn, synchronised inside), the command Cmd_RxReset and the new status outputs and events (Stat_TxBufErr, Stat_RxResetDone, Stat_RxResetBusy, Stat_CdrLock, Stat_RxElecIdle, Ev_RxReset, Ev_RxResetTimeout), one to one with the core. Stat_RxBufErr moves from the Stat interface to the Phy interface (rx_buf_err); a system that exported it with Stat reads it in LANE_EVENTS of the core instead.

The falling edge of Phy_CdrEnable (the lane leaves the states that use the line) starts the entire receiver reset of the lane (PA-IF-02, PA-RS-04); the CDR is held while the receiver reports electrical idle (PA-IF-04). The new source hdl/ofb_pa_gty/src/ofb_pa_gty_lane_rst.vhd is in both file lists of the adapter. The wizard instance needs the reset, CDR and debug ports of tcl/ofb_gtw.tcl of this version: create it again.

changes.text: The error recovery buffer registers every admitted data word with its row write and the commit of its item (DL-ER-09), so every item reaches the transmitter one CoreClk cycle later: a packet of one byte on the idle link takes 370, 393, 400 and 402 ns with 1, 2, 3 and 4 lanes (user guide section 7).

blocks.name: CCSDS 123.0-B-2 compressor
blocks.summary: Lossless and near-lossless compression of multispectral and hyperspectral images (CCSDS 123.0-B-2) with all predictors, quantizers and entropy coders of the standard; every parameter is a generic (with RuntimeConfig_g the image dimensions and the band-independent error limit values of every image come from configuration ports, with RuntimeParams_g also the user-defined data, M, the weight update and the entropy coder parameters), the header of the compressed image follows from them.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true. A reset aborts the image in progress.

Every image is compressed independently with the same parameters (with RuntimeConfig_g its own dimensions and error limit values from Cfg, with RuntimeParams_g also its own parameters from Params); the samples of the next image may follow the last sample of an image without a gap.
The decompressor must know the tables that are not in the header (table generics false) and the initial accumulators of the hybrid coder.
With RuntimeParams_g in BI order the throughput budget holds for M = SubFrameDepth_g, the maximum; an image with a smaller M has the throughput of its M (user guide section 4.5).
The hybrid coder is decoded from the end of the compressed image; keep Out_Last (the end of the packet) up to the decompressor.
After a detected double error (Ecc_Ded) the compressed image in progress may be wrong; discard it and reset the core before the next image.
With UseInLast_g, In_Last accompanies the last sample of every image; otherwise every image is flagged and the samples up to the next In_Last are discarded.

With UseInLast_g, an In_Last before the last sample aborts the image with that sample (sample L of the image in its input order, counted from 0): an aborted image is the compressed image of the samples taken; a decoder that is given the number of samples taken (L + 1) decodes it; the header announces the complete image. Its bytes do not depend on the timing of the input or the output.

With PeriodicUpdate_g the core takes no error limit value for three clock cycles after an early In_Last; a source that delivers the values ahead drops the remaining values of the aborted image within two clock cycles of Ev_ImageError and continues with the next image.
Enable the TMR of the synthesis tool for the core; it protects its memories itself and relies on TMR for all other logic (user guide section 6).

blocks.name: CCSDS 123.0-B-2 compression channel
blocks.summary: The compressor of ocp_core for a system: the samples of the images arrive as SDUs on a byte stream, for example from a receive port of OpenSPP, every compressed image leaves as one packet of a byte stream, and registers report the configuration (with RuntimeConfig_g they set the dimensions and error limits of every image, with RuntimeParams_g also the user-defined data, M, the weight update and the entropy coder parameters) and count the images, the faulty and discarded SDUs and the memory errors.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true. A reset aborts the image in progress and clears the counters.

Every SDU carries a whole number of samples and no other bytes (no secondary header): each sample in a big-endian container of cdiv(D, 8) bytes, the value in its D least significant bits. An SDU with a partial sample ends its image with an error.

The sender marks the last SDU of every image by the user signal (with OpenSPP: the CPTP User Application value, UserLastMask_g 22x"3FC000", UserLastValue_g 22x"004000" for the value 1); a faulty SDU (UserErrorMask_g, with OpenSPP 22x"003000") ends its image with an error and the SDUs after it up to the next end mark are discarded.

The status registers count the images (IMAGES_DONE, IMAGES_ABORTED), the faulty and the discarded SDUs (SDU_ERRORS, SDUS_DISCARDED) and the memory errors (ECC_CORRECTED, ECC_UNCORRECTABLE); every counter saturates and a write clears it. IMAGES_DONE + IMAGES_ABORTED is the number of compressed images output.
An image that ended with a faulty last SDU is complete and has the bytes of a good image; a receiver that must know the faulty images uses Out_Error or the counters.

An end mark or a faulty SDU before the last sample aborts the image with the last sample taken (sample L of the image in its input order, counted from 0; the samples of a faulty SDU are taken, an incomplete last container as one sample): an aborted image is the compressed image of the samples taken; a decoder that is given the number of samples taken (L + 1) decodes it; the header announces the complete image. Its bytes do not depend on the timing of the input or the output.

With PeriodicUpdate_g the channel takes no error limit value for three clock cycles after the last sample taken of an aborted image; a source that delivers the values ahead drops the remaining values of the aborted image within two clock cycles of Ev_ImageError and continues with the next image.
The source starts after the reset of the channel with the first SDU of an image; an image in progress at the end of the reset is aborted at its end mark.
The decompressor must know the tables that are not in the header (table generics false) and the initial accumulators of the hybrid coder.
With RuntimeParams_g in BI order the throughput budget holds for M = SubFrameDepth_g, the maximum; an image with a smaller M has the throughput of its M (user guide section 4.5).
The hybrid coder is decoded from the end of the compressed image; keep the end of the packet (Out_Last) up to the decompressor.
After a detected double error (Ecc_Ded) the compressed image in progress may be wrong; discard it and reset the channel before the next image.
Enable the TMR of the synthesis tool for the channel; ocp_core protects its memories itself, the adapters and the status registers rely on TMR like all other logic (user guide section 6).

Read ID (0x000) = 0x4F435003 to identify the channel. Before the first sample of an image write NEXT_X (0x068), NEXT_Y (0x06C), NEXT_Z (0x070) and NEXT_LIMITS (0x074), then CONTROL.COMMIT (0x060); STATUS (0x064) shows CFG_ERROR for a value out of range and CFG_PENDING until the next image start.

blocks.name: AES-GCM core
blocks.summary: AES-GCM authenticated encryption and decryption (FIPS 197, NIST SP 800-38D, CCSDS 352.0-B-2) with a key table, IV generation per key slot and a register file; one message per context, one status per message.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen with SyncTmr_g = true.
After the reset the key table erases every slot (NumKeys_g cycles, STATUS.BUSY = '1'); no key survives a reset.
One context per message, in the order of the messages; the core pairs the n-th context with the n-th message.
Load every key slot in use through the registers before sending contexts (programming sequence of the user guide).
Without the release buffer, discard every decrypted message whose last beat carries the error flag or whose status is not OK.
Save the invocation counter of every slot with generated IVs regularly ahead of the operational value (GCM 9.1).

rules.message: the AES engine sustains one beat per cycle with ceil(Nr / R) round units and has Nr rounds
the pacer of the key table scrubbers counts milliseconds
the release buffer holds a power of two of at least 16 beats
Set DenseOutput_g = true, so that every message leaves as one gapless byte string (IV, AAD, ciphertext, tag); the sectioned output is for the input of a second core (decryption).

The error flag of the messages (user bit 2 on the last beat) is not passed on, so a message that failed (for example with KEY) is sent like a good one. Set ReleaseBuffer_g = true (a message leaves the core only when its status is OK) with ReleaseBytes_g a power of two that holds the longest message in whole beats (IV, AAD, data and tag each start a new beat), or consume the status at M_Sts.

init.text: After the reset wait until STATUS (0x014) bit 0 BUSY is 0: the key table erases every slot.

Load every key slot in use: write the key to KEY0 to KEY7 (0x040 + 4 n; key byte 4 n in bits 31:24; 4, 6 or 8 words), for generated IVs the fixed field to IV_FIXED (0x060) and the first invocation counter to IV_COUNT_LO (0x064) and IV_COUNT_HI (0x068), then write KEY_LOAD (0x06C) with START (bit 31), IV_GEN (bit 8) and the slot (bits 7:0), for example 0x80000100 for slot 0 with generated IVs; wait until STATUS.BUSY is 0.

blocks.endToEnd: Load the key slot, send a packet and check the output: with generated IVs the first 4 bytes of every message are IV_FIXED, the next 8 the invocation counter; decrypt it with AES-GCM in the test bench (or a second core) and compare.

rates.evidence: TC-CO-10 and TC-CO-11 (back-to-back encryptions and decryptions without stall cycles, hdl/ocr_core/docs/verification_report.md)

M_Out.cycles: DenseOutput_g * (cdiv(n, B) + 1) + (1 - DenseOutput_g) * (cdiv(12, B) + cdiv(n - 28, B) + cdiv(16, B))

blocks.name: Chunk framer
blocks.summary: Cuts packets of any length into chunks of ChunkBytes_g bytes and hands every chunk to the AES-GCM core as one encryption with a generated IV and a 4-byte AAD with the position of the chunk in its packet.
notes: The slot Cfg_Slot is loaded for generated IVs and stays unchanged while the framer holds chunks.
Every chunk consumes one invocation of the slot; save the counter regularly (GCM 9.1).
A receiver decrypts every chunk on its own (IV bytes 0 to 11, AAD bytes 12 to 15, tag the last 16 bytes), orders the chunks by the invocation counter and finds the packet boundaries in the positions.

rules.message: The framer and the core share clock and reset; a reset of only one of them leaves contexts or messages without partner.

init.text: Load the key slot Cfg_Slot of the AES-GCM core for generated IVs (KEY_LOAD with IV_GEN = '1', see the core) before the first packet; without a loaded slot every chunk fails with KEY.

blocks.name: SpaceFibre port
blocks.summary: SpaceFibre node interface of one port according to ECSS-E-ST-50-11C: virtual channels and broadcast messages, Data Link, Multi-Lane and Lane layers and the Management Information Base, for 1 to 4 lanes. The physical adapter (transceivers) is a separate block.
notes: The VC ports have the link format of OpenSPP: spp_core with DataWidth_g = 32 x NumLanes_g connects to a VC port directly (M_Link_User(0) to S_Vc_TUser); the further user bits of OpenSPP (destination index) do not reach the SpaceFibre port.
Every VC carries any packets; which VC carries which traffic is a convention of the system that both ends of the link follow.
Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool (Vivado FSM_SAFE_STATE = default_state on the state registers, Synplify syn_encoding = safe).

Read ID and GENERICS after the reset; start the link with LANE_CTRL = 0x63 at one end (LaneStart, AutoStart, TxEn, RxEn), or with LaneStart_g = true at that end, and wait for DL_STATUS bits 1:0 = 3 (programming sequence of the user guide).
All four clocks must run for the reset to complete; CoreClk may be the lane clock (as in the VCK190 reference design).

rules.message: the output VC buffer holds a data frame of 64 words (VcOutDepth_g x NumLanes_g, DL-VO-05)
the error recovery buffer holds a data frame of 64 rows (DL-ER-08)
CoreClk must run at least as fast as LaneClk; a slower CoreClk loses received rows (DL_ERRORS bit 10).
UserClk slower than LaneClk limits the throughput of the virtual channels (one beat of NumLanes_g words per cycle).
the alignment watchdog is 0 (off) or at least 1024 lane clock cycles (ML-AL-11)
the join hold is at most the alignment watchdog AlignTimeoutWords_g while the watchdog is on (ML-LM-17)
with several lanes the input VC buffer holds two flow control units (DL-VI-05); reference value 256 x NumLanes_g

constraints.note: Clock crossings inside the core (Open Logic): for every pair of its clocks, in both directions, the period of the faster clock.

init.text: Start the link at one end: write LANE_CTRL (0x100 + 0x20 i) of every lane i = 0x63 (LaneStart, AutoStart, TxEn, RxEn), or 0x62 (AutoStart, TxEn, RxEn) to wait for the far end.
Start the link at one end: write LANE_CTRL (0x100 + 0x20 i) of every lane i = 0x63 (LaneStart, AutoStart, TxEn, RxEn); the reset value 0x62 (AutoStart, AutoStart_g) starts when the far end sends.
The lanes start after the reset without software (LaneStart_g, LANE_CTRL reset value 0x61 or 0x63).
Wait for LANE_STATUS (0x104 + 0x20 i) bits 3:0 = 7 (Active) of the lanes and DL_STATUS (0x010) bits 1:0 = 3 (link initialised); VC_HAS_CREDIT (0x030) shows the VCs that may send.

blocks.endToEnd: Connect two nodes (in a simulation without the transceiver models: the ofb_pa_gty of both ends in the architecture mdl, hdl/ofb_pa_gty/compile_order_sim.txt of OpenFibre, with the serial pins of the two ends crossed), start the link at one end and send a packet on a virtual channel; it arrives on the same virtual channel at the other end.

rates.evidence: user guide section 7; TC-NI-07 (virtual channel ports), TC-CORE-16 (link efficiency), TC-CORE-15 (CoreClk); rowEff derived from the link efficiency of TC-CORE-16 (words of 4 bytes, packets of 1 to 1024 B) and the row model of TC-NI-07

links.note: measured with packets of 1 to 1024 B, conservative above

sizes.evidence: no length limit by design: segments are independent of packet boundaries (ofb_dl_vc_out.vhd, DL-VO-03 and DL-VO-04), no length counter in NI, DL or MIB; packets of 65542 bytes (the largest Space Packet) with 1 to 4 lanes (TC-CORE-20, user guide section 7)

blocks.name: SpaceFibre GTY adapter
blocks.summary: Physical adapter of OpenFibre for one AMD Versal GTY quad (vendor-specific): 8B/10B, comma alignment and receive clock correction in the transceivers at 6.25 Gbit/s. Its lane clock output is the lane clock of the core.
notes: Vendor-specific (AMD Versal GTY). Its entity (hdl/ofb_pa_gty/src/ofb_pa_gty.vhd), its lane reset sequencer (hdl/ofb_pa_gty/src/ofb_pa_gty_lane_rst.vhd) and its architecture struct (hdl/ofb_pa_gty/src/ofb_pa_gty_struct.vhd) are not in compile_order.txt of the repository but in hdl/ofb_pa_gty/compile_order.txt: add them to the library openfibre after the core, and create the transceiver wizard instance ofb_gtw in the Vivado project with hdl/ofb_pa_gty/tcl/ofb_gtw.tcl (source the file, then ofb_gtw_create ofb_gtw 156.25 for a 156.25 MHz reference clock or ofb_gtw_create ofb_gtw 100 for 100 MHz).
RefClk is the output O of the IBUFDS_GTE5 of the reference clock pins of the quad; place the buffer in the chip-level top, as hdl/ofb_vck190/src/ofb_vck190_top.vhd does.

Stat_TxReady reaches Phy_TxReady of the core through the Phy interface; the core holds the link in Near-End Reset while the transmitters are not ready, so its reset needs no status of the adapter. The VCK190 reference design resets the core and the adapter with the power-on reset.
The line rate is 6.25 Gbit/s, so LaneClk runs at 156.25 MHz; the reference clock is 100 MHz or 156.25 MHz, the frequency the wizard instance is created for (PA-CK-01).

Phy_NoSignal is always 0 (PA-IF-03): the receiver of the transceiver gives no loss of signal indication at 6.25 Gbit/s, so a lost signal reaches the Lane layer as words with errors (RXERR), and an end with AutoStart leaves Wait at once and starts like an end with LaneStart.

Phy_CdrEnable does not stop the clock data recovery: its falling edge, when the lane leaves the states that use the line, starts the entire receiver reset of the lane (PA-IF-02, PA-RS-04; PA_CTRL RX_RESET_ON_DISCONNECT of the core), and LANE_CTRL RX_RESET of the core requests one. The adapter drops further requests of the lane for RxRstGapCycles_g after a reset, so that a lane with the initialisation timeout of the standard makes initialisation attempts between two resets; a design with a longer timeout (InitTimeoutWords_g of the core, LANE_INIT_TIMEOUT) sets RxRstGapCycles_g = 0, as the VCK190 reference design does. The CDR is held while the receiver reports electrical idle (PA-IF-04, PA_CTRL CDR_HOLD_IDLE).

The architecture struct needs the AMD transceiver models in a simulation (unisim and the simulation files of the wizard; OpenFibre runs them with tools/run_xsim.py). GHDL and QuestaSim simulate the adapter with its behavioural model, the architecture mdl in plain VHDL: hdl/ofb_pa_gty/compile_order_sim.txt lists it instead of struct, with the 8B/10B package, ofb_pa_model_pkg (ModelIdx_g selects the control record of an instance) and the lane reset sequencer, which the model uses as well. QuestaSim needs a time resolution of 1 fs (vsim -t fs) when the reference clocks of the ends differ by fractions of a picosecond, for example a few hundred ppm.

blocks.name: RMAP node
blocks.summary: RMAP target and initiator according to ECSS-E-ST-50-52C on SpaceWire packet ports, with a memory master, a pass-through port for other protocols and a register file.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
M_RepData, M_Conf and M_User must be served when connected; a stalled output stalls the received packet stream and the link.

With AxiMaxBeats_g = 1 and AxiDataWidth_g = 32 the memory master issues single transfers only and can drive an AXI4-Lite slave; tie M_Axi_RLast to '1'.

The RMAP node normally runs on the user clock of its SpaceWire port; an asynchronous FIFO was inserted instead.

init.text: After the reset wait until TABLE_STATUS (0x040) bits 1:0 (TX_BUSY, RX_BUSY) are 0: the core initialises both APID tables (2048 clock cycles).

Nothing else is needed: with TxPathDefault_g and RxPathDefault_g every APID has an enabled path to destination 0 and to receive port 0, destination 0 has the Target Logical Address 0xFE (DEST_CTRL 0x400) and the own address is Tla_g. A flight configuration writes the APID tables (TX_TABLE_APID 0x030 and TX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x034, RX_TABLE_APID 0x038 and RX_TABLE_ENTRY 0x03C) and the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

Enable the managed data paths: for every APID write TX_TABLE_APID (0x030), read TX_TABLE_ENTRY (0x034), write it with ENABLE and DEST, read it again; the same with RX_TABLE_APID (0x038) and RX_TABLE_ENTRY (0x03C) with ENABLE and PORT; write the destinations (DEST_CTRL 0x400 + 0x20 n).

blocks.endToEnd: Send one SDU on a send port (APID 0x123, for example) and expect it on receive port 0 with the same APID in user bits 10:0, once the APID tables are ready.
